name: liblo
why: A lightweight Open Sound Control implementation, a door into the networked protocol musicians use to drive synths and software.

brief.what_it_is: liblo is a C library implementing Open Sound Control (OSC), a networked message protocol that musicians use to drive synths and software. Programs link against it to send and receive OSC messages on POSIX systems, and the project says it is portable to most UNIX systems including OS X, and to Windows. The homepage also describes Windows and Android build notes and related bindings for Perl, Python, and asyncio. The brew executables listed (oscdump, oscsend, oscsendfile) are not described in either page I read, so their behaviour is unverified here.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes liblo as a library that provides an easy to use implementation of the OSC protocol. The homepage calls it a lightweight OSC implementation for POSIX systems.
brief.how_it_works: liblo is built as a dynamically-linked library, and the README says applications must install it with make install so the library can be found at runtime. Its servers can listen with either poll() or select(), with poll() as the default. The README also says the library supports IPv4 and IPv6, with IPv6 disabled by default.

commands_seen.context: GitHub README, CMake build: creates a separate build directory for liblo.
GitHub README, CMake build: initialises CMake from the source tree in place of the configure step.
GitHub README, CMake build: compiles liblo after CMake has been set up.
GitHub README, configure build: installs liblo so applications can locate the library.
GitHub README, Debugging: compiles liblo with debugging flags.
GitHub README, IPv6 notice: turns on IPv6 support, which is off by default.
GitHub README, Poll vs Select: disables poll() support so the select() code path is used, which the README says is faster on macOS.
GitHub README, Poll vs Select: the CMake equivalent of --disable-poll.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with ./configure and make, or with CMake (for Visual Studio on Windows, use CMake, per build/README.md in the repo). Run make install so applications can find the library. Man pages and PostScript docs are not shipped in the tarball; the homepage says they are built from the source tarball with doxygen. No accounts, runtimes or hardware are needed. Notes for Windows and Android are on the homepage.
brief.standout: It is a small, portable, C-level OSC library with no runtime dependencies named in the README, and the examples are designed to run without installation via a wrapper script. The README's IPv6 notice is candid: most OSC software such as Pd and SuperCollider does not listen on IPv6 sockets, so the default is off.
brief.status: Maintained, by the evidence I could read. The homepage names Stephen Sinclair as the current maintainer and lists liblo 0.36 as the latest stable release. The GitHub README says the GitHub repo is preferred for active development. I did not find a release date or last commit date, so recency is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: Licence is LGPL 2.1 or later; the homepage says closed-source use must link dynamically. The IPv6 support is off by default because of interoperability problems. poll() vs select() performance differs by platform. The homepage says the SourceForge git repo is synced manually. The brew executables oscdump, oscsend and oscsendfile were not documented in the pages I read, so I could not describe their options.
